performers: The Tudor Consort; Alastair Carey, director
intro: A bird flits from fir to beech to myrtle, singing of love. In Monteverdi’s five-part madrigal, the Tudor Consort passes its quick notes from voice to voice.

sections.label: A · Three high voices sing the bird
sections.mNote: Two sopranos and alto share the quick figures

sections.label: B · Five voices, a declaration of love
sections.mNote: Tenor and bass join the upper singers

sections.label: C · The bird receives a blessing
sections.mNote: Running notes extend the final words

cues.title: A bird in three voices
cues.text: Two sopranos and an alto begin; tenor and bass wait. The upper singers share quick runs on the words for singing and flying. Monteverdi gives his little bird three throats.
cues.evidence: Daniel Van Gilst’s edition (2019), bars 1–17: the upper trio sets the bird’s song and flight before the lower parts enter. https://ks15.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/b/b7/IMSLP561996-PMLP525417-Monteverdi,_Claudio_-_Quel_augellin_che_canta_(5vx).pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Guarini’s amorous bird
cues.text: In Guarini’s Il pastor fido, a bird flies between a fir, a beech and a myrtle. If it could speak, it would declare that it burns with love. Its mate answers in the same spirit; the human speaker blesses the little bird.
cues.evidence: Guarini, Il pastor fido, Act I, scene 1, lines 175–186, with Monteverdi’s adapted ending in the 1603 madrigal. LiederNet gives the original and sung texts. https://www.lieder.net/lieder/get_text.html?RF=0&TextId=7068

cues.title: The little bird lingers
cues.text: The final blessing keeps the bird in the air. Quick notes spread across the upper voices while the bass holds longer notes below. The last words, vago augelletto — lovely little bird — stretch through phrase after phrase.
cues.evidence: Van Gilst’s edition (2019), bars 59–74, setting “amoroso, gentil, vago augelletto”; translation ours. https://ks15.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/b/b7/IMSLP561996-PMLP525417-Monteverdi,_Claudio_-_Quel_augellin_che_canta_(5vx).pdf
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: The lower voices join the bird
transitions.from: A · Three high voices sing the bird
transitions.to: B · Five voices, a declaration of love
transitions.how: Tenor and bass turn the opening trio into five-part singing. The poem moves from the bird’s flight to its imagined declaration of love. The bass has longer notes beneath the sopranos’ running phrases, and the voices bring their declarations to a shared close.
transitions.evidence: Van Gilst’s edition (2019), bars 17–31, the lower entries and setting of “s’avesse umano spirto” and “ardo d’amore”. https://ks15.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/b/b7/IMSLP561996-PMLP525417-Monteverdi,_Claudio_-_Quel_augellin_che_canta_(5vx).pdf

transitions.title: The blessing grows new wings
transitions.from: B · Five voices, a declaration of love
transitions.to: C · The bird receives a blessing
transitions.how: The blessing begins in the three upper voices. Tenor and bass rejoin, and the word vago grows into long runs passed among the singers. Beneath them the bass moves in slower notes, carrying the phrase towards its final held chord.
transitions.evidence: Van Gilst’s edition (2019), bars 44–74: upper-trio blessing, lower entries from bar 55 and the extended ending. https://ks15.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/b/b7/IMSLP561996-PMLP525417-Monteverdi,_Claudio_-_Quel_augellin_che_canta_(5vx).pdf

source.title: Monteverdi, Quel augellin che canta, ed. Daniel Van Gilst (2019), CC0
source.locator: Four-page score for two sopranos, alto, tenor and bass. The upper trio begins alone; tenor and bass join later.

timeline.note: Two sopranos and an alto share the bird’s quick figures; tenor and bass wait.

fields.label: Performers
fields.value: The Tudor Consort (vocal ensemble), Alastair Carey (director)
fields.note: The track description and Carey’s album notes agree. Five written parts do not establish five individual singers, and no instrumental players are credited.

fields.label: Work version
fields.note: The opened score supplies two soprano, alto, tenor and bass parts, without instruments. Neither the exact edition used by the choir nor its performance transposition is established.

fields.label: Recorded
fields.note: The track names the Ordizia concert; the album’s first-person liner notes explicitly date it to Wednesday 2 November 2005. The 19 August 2010 date on FMA and Commons is an online release, not the recording session.

fields.label: Place
fields.note: The track and album notes name the venue. The later Rome concert and 2006 New Zealand recording described elsewhere in the same album notes belong to different tracks.

fields.label: Label
fields.note: The album was prepared for the Tudor Consort’s twentieth anniversary, but no original imprint is named. FMA and Commons are access repositories.

fields.label: Catalogue
fields.note: No commercial catalogue number is supplied.

fields.label: Matrix, take, sides
fields.note: The notes refer to a disc but supply no matrix, mastering identifier or take number.

fields.label: Transfer
fields.value: Timothy Hurd, producer and engineer; Commons import by ComputerHotline
fields.note: Hurd is explicitly credited at album level. The Commons uploader is not presented as the original engineer.

fields.label: Transfer date
fields.note: The 2005 concert date, 2010 FMA release and 11 April 2020 Commons upload do not establish a mastering or transfer date.

fields.label: Processing
fields.value: FMA MP3 source converted to Ogg for Commons; Wikimedia MP3 access derivative
fields.note: Original recording medium, microphones, editing and equalisation settings are not supplied. No further processing or audio trim is introduced here.

fields.label: Composition rights
fields.value: Public-domain 1603 madrigal; inspected engraving dedicated under CC0
fields.note: Historical composition rights and Van Gilst’s engraving status are separate from the Tudor Consort’s sound recording rights.

fields.label: Recording rights
fields.note: The external FMA track was opened directly and explicitly licenses this human choral performance under CC BY 3.0, without a NonCommercial condition. Commons contains a 2024 review template referring anomalously to a Flickr image; that text is not relied upon as verification of an FMA recording. The actual FMA recording page supplies independent evidence.

dossier.credit: Monteverdi, Quel augellin che canta, SV 87; The Tudor Consort, directed by Alastair Carey. Recorded live, Parroquial Church, Ordizia, Spain, 2 November 2005. Timothy Hurd, producer and engineer. Source: The Tudor Consort / Free Music Archive; Commons import by ComputerHotline. Recording CC BY 3.0; transcoded access copy, no new editorial audio cut.
